note: Attacker-controlled input of 32768 bytes is copied into the 32768-byte global buffer static_data. The input starts with three single-quote characters (''' ) followed by 32765 'a' characters.
The config parser is initialized with the attacker-controlled buffer. config_init_data sets lexer->end = static_data + size - 1 = static_data + 32767.
The dump function starts reading configuration lines, which drives the parser through lex_next and into the lexer state machine.
parse_key_value calls lex_next to obtain the first lexeme from the attacker-controlled input.
lex_next invokes the current lexer state function, which is lex_config, to begin tokenizing the input.
lex_config reads the first character which is a single quote. strncmp(lexer->pos, "''", 2) matches the next two quote characters, so lex_multiline_string is entered.
peek(lexer) returns the second quote character, so end is set to the string "'''" (three single quotes).
advance_n advances lexer->pos by 2, so lexer->pos now points to static_data + 3, just past the opening triple-quote.

The loop repeatedly calls strncmp(lexer->pos, "'''", 3) to look for the closing triple-quote. Since the remaining input is all 'a' characters, no match is found and next() advances lexer->pos one byte at a time.

After many iterations, lexer->pos reaches static_data + 32766 (which is lexer->end - 1). strncmp reads 3 bytes starting here: static_data[32766], static_data[32767], and static_data[32768]. The read at static_data[32768] is 1 byte past the end of the 32768-byte global buffer, causing a global-buffer-overflow READ of 1 byte.
